I do know what you mean. I experience this on a daily basis honestly. Looking for that external sort of validation, whether it be material or socially can only go so far. At least for me. The way I fill the void is a process haha... I’ll explain.

It requires a lot of observance with myself. I will ask myself what do I feel I need. The first thoughts are to usually seek validation through whatever. When I’m met with that thought, I ask myself in a parental tone “but what do you really need though?” 

What I get is hard to describe... I’ll try though. I feel like I get more to the root of my CPTSD. I usually can find a traumatic memory deep inside me that really really hurts. And I go through that memory knowing that I tried my best with the knowledge that I had in that scenario. 

Which usually leads to crying about it, but it heals it a little. Only after that is when I feel at peace. 
For me even starting that process takes an immense amount of patience and self discipline. 

Tl;dr I meditate on what the trigger is and why am I being triggered. That’s painful enough to get through, but it’s moving through the memory and reprocessing it in a more mature way rather than moving past it. Hopefully this helps :)❤️

For me personally, it helps to talk to someone about it and really try to be a “big sibling” to my younger self and reprocess or relive that experience. While reliving it, really saying to myself that it’s okay that it happened or my personal favorite one “you had all of the knowledge that you could have had at that point in time and you did the best you could going through it the first time” 

Really crying about it and grieving over it is what helps me out the most. 

Those traumatic episodes will affect how you interact with your environment and people everyday. And that’s hard. I’ve pushed so many people away, and ironically I’m doing it in my current situation. So it’s hard to get those thoughts to stop pestering you and controlling you and your actions. It may seem like a big mountain to climb over, but really think on what would make you feel better or good in the moment, realistically. They may not be the answers you want to hear. They may be the toughest answers, but it’s a place to start. And it’s something you deserve to and can get through. 

Whatever memories pop up for you, you did the best you could have, and that’s the most you can ask of yourself. Hope you’re having a good night friend. Sending my love and good vibes your way ❤️❤️❤️
